elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 as redlined reads "Customer has no obligation to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier," converting the affirmative MFN covenant into an express negation. No other provision imposes a match, best-terms, or no-less-favourable obligation on Customer, and Section 12.3 is retained and reinforces that Customer "has made no ... most-favoured-customer ... commitment."

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer MFN obligation at all (Section 7.2 negated; Section 12.3 confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment), so a product-scope limitation is unnecessary and the fallback constraint is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no MFN obligation runs against Customer post-edit, so there is no duration to cap; the outcome is stricter than a 12-month limit.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the obligation eliminated there is no comparison mechanic requiring like-for-like carve-outs.

reasons: The single operation targets only the offending words in Section 7.2 and achieves the preferred position by negating the Customer-side MFN; no survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or other extras were added.

Section 12.3 and all surrounding commercial mechanics are left untouched, and the edit removes the direct conflict between the former Section 7.2 covenant and Vendor's acknowledgement in Section 12.3 that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
No Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour existed in the cited text, so none was disturbed; the redline does not delete any Customer-favourable language.
The edit leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference: Section 7.2 remains a complete, self-contained sentence after the change.
